exposure: Continuous epidural block combined with free positioning during labor
Continuous epidural block combined with routine obstetric positioning during labor
outcome: Duration of labor (first, second, third, and total stages)
Sense of control during childbirth (internal, external, total scores)
Fear of childbirth (neonatal health, delivery control, pain, hospital intervention, total scores)
cohort: The study included 146 women undergoing vaginal delivery, randomly divided into a control group and a research group (n=73 each).
finding: Continuous epidural block combined with free positions significantly shortened labor duration, reduced neonatal asphyxia and genital tract injury rates, increased sense of control, and eased fear of childbirth and postpartum fatigue compared to routine positioning.
mod_finding: The research group (free positions) had a higher natural delivery rate and lower rates of conversion to cesarean section and assisted vaginal delivery.
